# agentpc

agentpc gives AI agents instant, resettable Windows, Ubuntu and Arch Linux ARM desktop VMs on an Apple Silicon Mac, through one MCP server (`agentpc mcp`).

The VMs are ARM64. x64 Windows apps run through Prism; x86_64 and i386 Linux programs and amd64 containers run in the `ubuntu-x86apps` and `arch-x86apps` images, through FEX. Hardware TSO (macOS 15+) is reported as `x86_tso` in `list_vms`; on Arch, `sudo fex-pacman -Sy --noconfirm --needed <pkg>` adds x86 packages. The `arch` guest (Arch Linux ARM) is like Ubuntu, with Chromium as its browser and pacman (`sudo pacman -Syu --noconfirm <pkg>`) for packages.

## VM Creation and Viewing

`create_vm` returns once the desktop is ready. A named create retried in the same session returns the same VM; use a unique name per task. `open_in_browser: true` opens the ready VM's viewer in the Mac's default browser, not a browser inside the guest. It defaults to false and is a per-call action, not a saved VM setting; a browser-launch failure warns without failing creation. Use it when the user asks to watch the VM. CLI equivalent: `agentpc create ubuntu --open` (alias `--open-in-browser`).

Dated image tags (`…-YYYYMMDD`) select a published build and are download-only. An image push updates rolling tags but preserves existing dated tags; a refreshed rolling image can differ from its dated build. Publishers on different machines must serialize publication for a new date unless the registry enforces immutable tags.

## Commands, jobs and looking

`run_command` returns typed `structuredContent` (its `outputSchema`) next to the readable `exit code: N` text. Nonzero exits, timeouts and lost connections are tool errors. At a foreground run's `timeout` agentpc attempts to stop it and keeps its partial output; `termination_confirmed` says whether agentpc verified that none of the processes it identified is left (best effort on Windows; not a sandbox guarantee), and an unconfirmed stop, or a lost connection before the command's end was known (`connection_lost` with `effect_unknown: true`), sets `effect_unknown` and a `job_id` for `get_job_status` / `stop_job`. Commands are never retried automatically.

`get_job_status` takes `wait_seconds` (0 to 30, default 0; a wait never stops the job) and `cursor` (a `next_cursor` or `"start"`; at most 16 KiB per reply, advancing by exactly the bytes returned, with an explicit `cursor_reset` when the log or VM changed). `inspect_desktop` is the read-only twin of `use_desktop_tool`: it runs only tools the VM's desktop driver explicitly marks read-only and refuses the rest before dispatching them. Full details: the MCP docs and AGENTS.md.

```sh
curl -fsSL https://agentpc.pawanpaudel.com.np/install.sh | sh
```
